findings.title: Parenthesis-depth claim about SQLite has no record
findings.description: The `MAX_DEPTH` comment states as fact that SQLite accepts 1001 pairs of parentheses, but no query or test in the PR measures this. The PR's measurement table covers unary operators and the height constructs, not parenthesis nesting, so the claim rests on assertion alone and the comment will mislead later readers if it is wrong.

findings.title: Comparison height rule for some operators is unverified
findings.description: The `comparison` and `equality` parsers apply the same height rule (highest operand plus 1) to `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==` and `!=` as to the operators that were measured. The PR's own report lists these five operators under "Not measured", and the `Node` comment in `src/select.rs` only records queries for `=`, `<>`, `<`, `IS NULL`, `OR` and `AND`. The ticket asks for the comparison height rule to be determined with `yt sqlite`, so these operators have no supporting query and result in the code or the PR.
